used.name: animate
used.read: §1 "Should this animate at all?" — the frequency table; §2 the six permitted purposes; §5 easing and duration; §7 reduced motion; "Never Ship"
used.principle: Decide whether it animates at all before deciding anything else, and let the frequency tier bound how much motion the moment may have.

used.name: animation-vocabulary
used.read: Glossary — "Looping & Ambient Motion"; "Polish & Effects"; "Transitions Between States"; "Principles to Know"
used.principle: Name the effect with the term the craft already has, so a direction can be checked against what it claims to be — and so a prohibited effect is recognised when it is arrived at under a friendlier name.

used.name: emil-design-eng
used.read: "Use blur to mask imperfect transitions"; "clip-path for Animation"; "Asymmetric enter/exit timing"; "Review Checklist"; "Debugging Animations"
used.principle: A transient blur bridges a crossing so the eye reads ONE transformation instead of two objects swapping. A clipped reveal produces a state change no per-property timing can match.

used.name: find-animation-opportunities
used.read: "Operating Posture" — expect to reject most candidates; "The Gate" §1 Frequency, §3 Speed, §4 Function; "Part 2 — Rejected candidates (REQUIRED)"
used.principle: Expect to reject most candidates, and PUBLISH the rejections. A moment that only works as a slow showy animation fails the gate.

used.name: animate-expo
used.read: §1 the two runtimes; §3 "Pick the tool" — the Skia row; §4 properties and BlurView; §8 haptics; §9 reduced motion; "Judging feel in Expo Go or the simulator"
used.principle: Keep motion on the UI runtime. Never animate a blur's intensity on Android. Feel is judged on a release build on the slowest device you support, and nothing else counts.

used.name: react-native-best-practices
used.principle: Software Mansion's production patterns; load the reference for the topic at hand.

used.name: react-native-best-practices/references/animations
used.principle: Load the reference for the question: Skia for canvas scenes, performance for fps and accessibility.

used.name: react-native-best-practices/references/animations/animations-performance.md
used.read: "Simultaneous Animation Limits"; "Prefer Non-Layout Properties"; "Accessibility" — useReducedMotion, ReducedMotionConfig, and the per-animation behaviour table
used.principle: Roughly 100 animated components on low-end Android and 500 on iOS; beyond that, Skia. Under reduced motion `withTiming` jumps to its target, entering animations jump to their endpoint, and `withRepeat` infinite DOES NOT START.

used.name: react-native-best-practices/references/animations/canvas-animations.md
used.read: "Reanimated Integration" — Group blendMode; "Color Interpolation" — interpolateColors; "Path Animations" — usePathValue / usePathInterpolation; "Rules" — Group transform origin, radians, Canvas accessibility
used.principle: Skia renders a whole scene to one canvas and Reanimated shared values drive its props directly. Its colour interpolation, transform origin and rotation units are NOT React Native's, and a direct port gets each of them wrong in a way that still renders.

used.name: react-native-best-practices/references/svg
used.principle: react-native-svg implements the SVG standard as a React component tree — so every element becomes a native view.

used.name: react-native-best-practices/references/animations/svg-animations.md
used.read: the whole file — createAnimatedComponent, animating a Path's `d`
used.principle: Animate SVG through `useAnimatedProps`, converting inside the callback.

used.name: apple-design
used.read: §2 direct manipulation; §3 interruptibility; §5 velocity handoff; §6 momentum projection; §11 frame-level smoothness; §14 reduced motion and accessibility; §16 the eight principles
used.principle: An interface feels alive when motion starts from the current on-screen value, inherits the user's velocity and projects momentum forward. Reduced motion means a gentler, non-vestibular equivalent — not no feedback.

used.name: frontend-design
used.read: "Design principles"; the calibration paragraph naming the three AI-default looks; "Restraint and self-critique"
used.principle: Spend your boldness in ONE place and let the signature element be the one memorable thing. Machine-generated design clusters around three looks, and one of them is a near-black background with a single bright accent.

used.name: designing-arabic-frontends
used.read: §1 declare an Arabic font; §2 line-height; §4 mixed-direction boundaries; §5 logical-first CSS; the letter-spacing and italics rules
used.principle: An Arabic UI is not a Latin UI with translated strings. Arabic needs ~1.6+ leading, never letter-spacing, and logical properties.

used.name: writing-eloquent-arabic
used.read: "Register: match the context"; the 8 failure modes — register-mismatch, english-word-order, calque, weak-connector
used.principle: Arabic composed by mapping an English sentence is grammatical and reads as translated. Compose in Arabic structure; lead with the verb; bind related ideas rather than stacking full stops.

used.name: fixing-accessibility
used.read: §1 accessible names; §4 semantics and heading levels; §7 contrast and states; §8 media and motion
used.principle: Prefer native semantics; never skip heading levels; every image carries alt text; respect prefers-reduced-motion for non-essential motion.

notUsed.name: improve-animations
notUsed.why: NOT APPLICABLE. It surveys an existing codebase's motion and produces an audit plus plans for other agents to execute. There is no codebase of motion here — D2 builds four moments from scratch on a selected language. Enumerated so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight.

notUsed.name: pulsar-haptics
notUsed.why: NOT APPLICABLE, DELIBERATELY. None of the four categories is user-initiated, and `animate-expo` §8 is explicit that a haptic fires one per user action and never on something the user did not cause. Recorded because a haptic on "QANDEEL understood something" is a real temptation and refusing it is a decision.

notUsed.name: impeccable
notUsed.read: the whole file — Setup, "How to design", Modes, Commands
notUsed.why: AVAILABLE AND DELIBERATELY NOT RUN. Its operating model is to establish or replace a project's design artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md) and, on its new-work path, to treat the incumbent look as "evidence and anti-reference". QANDEEL's visual world is frozen three tracks upstream and D2 is forbidden from treating it that way; running the skill as designed would have written project files this brief does not authorise. ONE PRINCIPLE WAS TAKEN FROM IT AND IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN CLAIMED AS USE: "verify in bounded passes, not a loop" — this package ran three bounded render-and-correct passes over the four categories and then stopped.

notUsed.name: design-critique
notUsed.why: NOT USED. It produces heuristic design feedback on a mockup. The critique D2 needed was of SEMANTIC TRUTH rather than usability heuristics, and that is what `D2R_TRUTH_AUDIT.md` is — written against the brief's own failure conditions, which are sharper here than a general heuristic set.

notUsed.name: user-research
notUsed.why: NOT APPLICABLE. No research was conducted and none is claimed.

unavailable.name: review-animations
unavailable.why: UNAVAILABLE — CANNOT BE INVOKED. Its frontmatter carries `disable-model-invocation: true`, so it cannot be run on this host. NO review-animations PASS WAS RUN ON THIS PACKAGE, and that is recorded rather than worked around. Its bar was applied through `animate` and `emil-design-eng`, which state the same rules, and every "Never Ship" row was walked by hand in §3.

unavailable.name: prototype
unavailable.why: UNAVAILABLE — CANNOT BE INVOKED. Also carries `disable-model-invocation: true`. It would have been genuinely useful: it builds several versions of a UI piece behind a picker to flip through live, which is close to what a four-category comparison wants. The substitute used instead was a single prototype with a switchable category and a capture harness that renders any of them to an exact millisecond — weaker for feel, stronger for evidence.

references.how: read in a browser; the page is client-rendered and returns an empty shell to a plain fetch
references.principle: "Add motion purposefully, supporting the experience without overshadowing it. Don't add motion for the sake of adding motion." / "In apps, generally avoid adding motion to UI interactions that occur frequently." / visionOS: avoid sustained oscillation, "in particular… around 0.2 Hz because people can be very sensitive to this frequency".
references.changed: The 0.2 Hz figure is the first of two independent sources naming the exact frequency a "breathing ring" would land on, and it is why the ambient field is still. "Avoid motion on frequently occurring interactions" is the same argument `animate`'s frequency table makes, from a second direction.
references.didNotChange: Nothing about the three meaning events. They are infrequent, purposeful and state-indicating, which is what this page asks for; it neither permits nor forbids anything D2 does with them.

references.principle: Under Reduce Motion, "ensure your app or game responds by reducing automatic and repetitive animations, including zooming, scaling, and peripheral motion", and specifically: "Replacing transitions in x-, y-, and z-axes with fades", "Avoiding animating into and out of blurs". Also: "Convey information with more than color alone."
references.changed: THE ONE REAL CONTRADICTION THIS GATE FOUND, and it is inside work that was already accepted. I-08B3.1-D1's reduced-motion counterpart KEEPS its bridging blur, for a good craft reason it states. This list says the opposite, in a document written for exactly this setting. D2 corrects that one channel — `source/scene/d2-connection.mjs`, check C2 — and reports it as a contradiction rather than folding it in. "More than colour alone" is why a topic's CONTOUR and its hue both come from the same identity.
references.didNotChange: The full-motion Connection, which is I-08B3.1-D1's function unmodified and is proved so at fourteen decimal places by check C1.

references.principle: M3 replaced its easing-and-duration system with springs in May 2025, and splits them: SPATIAL springs "overshoot the final value and bounce into place"; EFFECTS springs are for "color and opacity animations, where there shouldn't be any overshoot". Three speeds each, and "larger elements may use slow".
references.changed: TWO THINGS. First, it is the stated reason QANDEEL Light's intensity is a curve and not a spring: light intensity is an EFFECT in M3's own sense, and an overshoot there would be the insight arriving, retracting and arriving again. Second, the speed split is why PATTERN and INSIGHT run the shared lifecycle at 1.25x while CONNECTION runs at 1.0 — they are the larger elements, and that is a reason rather than a nudge for feel.
references.didNotChange: QANDEEL does not adopt the spring system. Its motion is system-initiated and non-interruptible by design, which is the case springs exist for and this one is not. Recorded as a divergence with its reason rather than passed over.

references.source: Software Mansion — React Native Reanimated, Accessibility
references.principle: `withTiming` and `withSpring` "return the toValue immediately"; entering, keyframe and layout animations "instantaneously reach their endpoints"; exiting animations and shared transitions "are omitted". `useReducedMotion` reports the setting AS IT WAS AT APP START.
references.changed: The reduced-motion counterparts are separate functions rather than a global flag, and `withDecay`'s documented behaviour — return the current value immediately — is implemented literally in the ambient pan: under reduced motion the map STOPS WHERE THE FINGER LET GO rather than gliding. That is the rule's real behaviour, not an approximation of it.
references.didNotChange: The full-motion expressions. Nothing here argues for changing what a user without the setting sees.

references.principle: Reanimated values are passed directly as Skia props — "no need for functions like createAnimatedComponent or useAnimatedProps" — and Skia ships its own `interpolateColors` because its colour storage differs from Reanimated's.
references.changed: Confirms the production path for the whole light layer runs on the UI thread with no bridge crossing per frame, and is the specific citation behind the colour-interpolation hazard in `D2R_IMPLEMENTATION_FEASIBILITY.md` §3.
references.didNotChange: Nothing visual. This is a route, not a design input.

references.principle: "The Atlas component is used for efficient rendering of multiple instances of the same texture or image", for "a very large number of similar objects", and "Atlas transforms can be animated with near-zero cost using worklets".
references.changed: THIS IS THE FEASIBILITY ANSWER FOR THE AMBIENT FIELD, and it arrived because the field was designed to need it. Because the contours are BUILD-TIME CONSTANTS, the whole field is a fixed set of sprites whose only per-frame change is a transform — which is precisely the case Atlas exists for. `D2R_IMPLEMENTATION_FEASIBILITY.md` §2.
references.didNotChange: The design. The field was already static before this was read; the reference told us what that buys, not what to draw.

references.source: Shopify — React Native Skia, Blur image filter
references.principle: Blur takes a Gaussian sigma and a TileMode; `decal` is the default and governs what happens where the kernel runs off the input.
references.changed: The light sources carry a 3.4 px Gaussian in this proof, which maps to a sigma and a tile mode rather than to a CSS filter; recorded in the port table with the note that `decal` is the correct mode for a source that must fade to nothing at its edge.
references.didNotChange: The magnitude. 3.4 px is a proof value and is listed as an implementation craft parameter, not a token.

references.source: Design Tokens Community Group — format specification status
references.how: fetched (the specification site itself could not be reached from this host — see below)
references.principle: The DTCG format reached STABLE at version 2025.10, published 2025-10-28.
references.changed: Confirms the version the emitted resolver declares. It is the same `$schema` and the same `version` string the FROZEN I-08B3.1-C3 resolver already carries, so D2 extends that tree at its own declared version rather than introducing a second one.
references.didNotChange: The token shapes, which are copied from the C3 tree's own conventions — the colour object with `colorSpace`, `components` and `hex`, the `{alias}` syntax, and `$extensions` for provenance.
references.limitation: HONESTLY RECORDED: `tr.designtokens.org` and `www.designtokens.org` could not be fetched or browsed from this host — one was refused outright and the others returned nothing. The structural authority actually used is therefore the frozen C3 token tree, which is a first-party artefact of this project and declares the 2025.10 schema itself. The clause-level spec text was NOT read for this package and is not claimed to have been.
